title: Digital to Wave 2 THz Validity: an engineering-validity study of the Part II THz human-wave interface equations
description:
Digital to Wave 2 THz Validity is a SYNTHETIC engineering-validity study, in Python (3.11–3.13), of the THz human-wave interface (HWI) equations in Mun Seok Lee's preprint Digital to Wave: LGD In Situ Wave Memory-Human Wave Integrated Interface-Metaverse Hologram- Wave Affective AI (Part II, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21947108). The preprint supplies the equations; the reference values, simulation choices, receivers, scoring and experiments are this project's own. Its author has not reviewed or endorsed this software.

What is included

  • An inventory of the quantitative content of Part II (and of the Part I p. 12 encoding) by PDF page, each item classified as (a) simulatable, (b) dimensionally or physically checkable, or (c) too vague to implement.
  • A dimensional check of each HWI equation (pp. 29–40) and an order-of-magnitude evaluation with cited standard reference values: THz absorption and refractive index of water, membrane thickness and permittivity, an extreme ZnTe-level second-order susceptibility upper bound, ICNIRP skin exposure limits, the breakdown field of air, heating, thermal times and the SNR condition.
  • A seeded, protocol-locked synthetic channel benchmark: the Part I signed-amplitude sine encoding (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21947036, p. 12; encoder and decoder vendored verbatim from the Digital to Wave Testbench v0.4.1, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23134616) passes through square-law rectification, a 100 Hz membrane low-pass, Beer–Lambert depth loss in water and two-tone THz beating, with nominal, calibrated and oracle receivers, Wilson intervals, closed-form predictions and exact McNemar tests.
  • Generated JSON/CSV/PNG artifacts with SHA-256 checksums, a pytest suite and CI on Python 3.11–3.13 that checks the vendored code against the upstream tag and regenerates every CSV and PNG byte for byte.

Results (SYNTHETIC; master seed 20261013, run from the protocol-lock commit)

  • Dimensional check: the Part II HWI equations on pp. 34–37 and p. 40 are consistent standard physics. The p. 29 “HWI Standard Equation” is not: its right side has units of J m−2, not W m−2.
  • With an extreme ZnTe-level χ(2) upper bound, reaching a 15 mV membrane threshold needs about 1013.8 W m−2 at the skin surface. That is about 1010.8 times the ICNIRP long-exposure skin limit, with an incident field about 76 times the breakdown field of air. It rises to 1023.4 W m−2 at 1 mm depth (water at 0.99 THz, penetration depth 45 µm).
  • Channel benchmark (passing frames out of 12,000): direct square-law rectification destroys the Part I sign (nominal 0 at every noise level). With the two-tone beat at noise SD 0.45 and 40 Hz, the nominal decoder passes 2,445 and the low-pass-calibrated receiver 10,743. At 60 Hz they pass 0 and 9,246. With noise SD 0.25, the depth-oracle receiver passes 12,000 at the surface, 9,749 at 30 µm, 892 at 50 µm and 0 at 100 µm. A relative THz tone error of 2.5×10−14 cuts the calibrated receiver to 4,433, and 5×10−14 cuts it to 0.
  • The closed-form predictions lie inside the pooled Wilson 95% intervals in 73 of 75 cells. The exceptions are one condition with 1 failure where 0.11 were expected.

Limits

No physical, biological or safety claim is made. The channel is dimensionless, the THz carrier is not sampled, the calibrated receiver is an oracle, and the susceptibility value is an extreme upper bound. The validity numbers are order-of-magnitude checks of printed equations, not a safety assessment.
